chosen: The street was empty.
rejected: Street was empty. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian lacks articles; English requires 'the' before a specific street being described]

chosen: She spoke with an accent.
rejected: She spoke with accent. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian lacks articles; English requires the indefinite article 'an' before 'accent' when referring to it non-specifically]

chosen: He wrote a letter to his friend.
rejected: He wrote letter to friend. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian lacks articles; English requires 'a letter' (indefinite) and 'his friend' (possessive) to form a grammatical sentence]

prompt: Они встретились у входа в театр.
a_side: Они встретились у входа в театр.
chosen: They met at the entrance to the theatre.
rejected: They met by entrance in theatre. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian 'у входа' is 'at the entrance'; 'в театр' is 'to the theatre'; articles and correct prepositions are required in English]

chosen: He left his keys at home.
rejected: He forgotten keys at home. [WRONG: morphological — simple past is 'forgot' or 'left'; 'forgotten' requires the auxiliary 'have'; the phrase 'left his keys' is more idiomatic than 'forgot his keys at home']

chosen: She dances well.
rejected: She dancings well. [WRONG: morphological — third person singular present is 'dances'; 'dancings' is not a valid form in any tense or mode]

chosen: The sky was blue.
rejected: Sky was bluish in colour. [WRONG: mistranslation — 'голубым' means 'blue' (specifically light blue in Russian); 'bluish' adds vagueness not present in the source; article 'the' is also missing]

chosen: He will call me in the evening.
rejected: He me will call evening. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian allows object pronoun before the verb; English requires strict subject-verb-object order; 'in the evening' requires the preposition 'in' and article 'the']

prompt: Он долго учился играть на гитаре.
a_side: Он долго учился играть на гитаре.
chosen: He spent a long time learning to play the guitar.
rejected: He long studied to play on guitar. [WRONG: literal calque — 'долго учился' is 'spent a long time learning'; 'на гитаре' is 'the guitar' (no 'on'); 'long studied' is not natural English word order]

chosen: I arrived first.
rejected: I came the first one. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian instrumental 'первым' (being first) in this context is simply 'first' as an adverb in English; 'the first one' is unnecessarily expanded]

chosen: She took him by the hand.
rejected: She took him for hand. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian 'за руку' means 'by the hand'; English requires 'by' not 'for', and the article 'the' before 'hand']

prompt: Он работает с восьми до пяти.
a_side: Он работает с восьми до пяти.
chosen: He works from eight to five.
rejected: He works from eight hours to five hours. [WRONG: literal calque — time expressions 'с восьми до пяти' are simply 'from eight to five'; adding 'hours' after each number is non-idiomatic in English time expressions]

chosen: She enrolled at university.
rejected: She entered into university. [WRONG: mistranslation — 'поступить в' for education means 'to enroll at/be admitted to'; 'entered into' suggests physically entering a building, not academic enrollment]

chosen: He went to get bread.
rejected: He went behind bread. [WRONG: literal calque — 'пойти за + instrumental' means 'to go to get something'; 'за' here is not a spatial preposition but a purposive one; 'went behind bread' is incoherent]

chosen: She waited for him for a whole hour.
rejected: She waited him whole hour. [WRONG: literal calque — 'ждать' requires 'wait for' + object in English; 'целый час' is 'for a whole hour'; missing prepositions and article]

chosen: He left three years ago.
rejected: He has gone away three years back. [WRONG: morphological — 'three years ago' is a specific completed past time reference; English uses simple past, not present perfect; 'back' for 'назад' is non-idiomatic in this construction]

chosen: They spoke in a low voice.
rejected: They conversated in quiet voice. [WRONG: morphological — 'conversated' is not a standard English past tense form; 'spoke' or 'talked' is correct; also 'in a quiet voice' is possible but 'in a low voice' is more idiomatic for hushed speaking]

chosen: He goes to school.
rejected: He studies himself in school. [WRONG: literal calque — reflexive 'учится' indicates the ongoing state of being a student; 'goes to school' is the natural English idiom; 'studies himself' is ungrammatical]

chosen: She watches television every evening.
rejected: She is watching television every evening. [WRONG: morphological — habitual routine actions use simple present in English; present continuous is incorrect for 'every evening' which marks a recurring habit]

chosen: We live in a small town.
rejected: We live in small town. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian lacks articles; English requires the indefinite article 'a' before singular countable noun phrases]

chosen: He failed the exam.
rejected: He falled through exam. [WRONG: mistranslation — 'провалить экзамен' means 'to fail an exam'; 'falled through' is not a valid English form; 'failed the exam' is the correct idiom]

chosen: I got lucky.
rejected: To me it luckied. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian impersonal 'мне повезло' uses the verb 'повезти' without a standard English equivalent verb; 'I got lucky' is the natural English equivalent; 'it luckied' is not a valid English construction]

chosen: It happened by accident.
rejected: It happened accidental. [WRONG: morphological — 'accidental' is an adjective; the adverb 'accidentally' or the phrase 'by accident' is required to modify the verb 'happened']

prompt: Он принимает лекарство трижды в день.
a_side: Он принимает лекарство трижды в день.
chosen: He takes the medicine three times a day.
rejected: He takes medicine three times in a day. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian 'в день' for frequency is 'a day' in English, not 'in a day'; also 'the medicine' requires the definite article for a specific prescribed medication]

chosen: Dear friend!
rejected: Expensive friend! [WRONG: false cognate — 'дорогой' means 'dear' as a term of address; its second meaning 'expensive' is irrelevant in a salutation; 'expensive friend' is an absurd rendering]

chosen: The lecture was boring.
rejected: The lection was boringly. [WRONG: false cognate — 'лекция' is 'lecture', not 'lection' (a reading from scripture); also 'boringly' is an adverb; the predicate adjective 'boring' is required after a copula]

chosen: She became a famous architect.
rejected: She became known architectress. [WRONG: mistranslation — 'известным' in this context means 'famous/well-known', not just 'known'; also 'architectress' is an archaic and rarely-used form; 'architect' is used for all genders; missing article 'a']

chosen: He plays the piano.
rejected: He plays on piano. [WRONG: literal calque — Russian 'играть на + instrument' corresponds to English 'play the + instrument'; the preposition 'on' is not used in English with musical instruments; the article 'the' is required]

chosen: She is afraid of the dark.
rejected: She fears darkness. [WRONG: register shift — 'fears' is more formal or literary; 'is afraid of' is the natural everyday English equivalent; also 'the dark' is the idiomatic form, not the abstract 'darkness']

chosen: You are right.
rejected: Thou art correct in thy assertion. [WRONG: register shift — 'ты прав' is an ordinary neutral-register statement; 'Thou art' is Early Modern English and is archaic; the correct modern English is 'You are right']

prompt: Она вернулась домой, приготовила ужин и легла спать.
a_side: Она вернулась домой, приготовила ужин и легла спать.
chosen: She came home, made dinner, and went to bed.
rejected: She came home. [WRONG: omission — the sentence contains three sequential actions; 'made dinner' and 'went to bed' were dropped; only the first action was translated]

prompt: Он читал книгу, пока шёл дождь.
a_side: Он читал книгу, пока шёл дождь.
chosen: He was reading a book while it was raining.
rejected: He read book. [WRONG: omission — the temporal clause 'while it was raining' was dropped; the book object also lost its article; both clauses are essential to the sentence]

prompt: Мы пошли в магазин, но он был закрыт.
a_side: Мы пошли в магазин, но он был закрыт.
chosen: We went to the shop, but it was closed.
rejected: We went to the shop. [WRONG: omission — the adversative clause 'but it was closed' was dropped; the contrast is the entire point of the sentence and must be included]

prompt: Если ты устал, ложись спать раньше.
a_side: Если ты устал, ложись спать раньше.
chosen: If you are tired, go to bed earlier.
rejected: Go to bed earlier. [WRONG: omission — the conditional clause 'if you are tired' was dropped; without the condition, the sentence becomes an unconditional command with a different meaning]

prompt: Несмотря на усталость, она продолжала работать.
a_side: Несмотря на усталость, она продолжала работать.
chosen: Despite her fatigue, she continued to work.
rejected: She continued to work. [WRONG: omission — the concessive phrase 'despite her fatigue' was dropped; it provides essential context showing her determination against a physical difficulty]

prompt: Екатерина Великая правила Россией в восемнадцатом веке.
a_side: Екатерина Великая правила Россией в восемнадцатом веке.
chosen: Catherine the Great ruled Russia in the eighteenth century.
rejected: Yekaterina Velikaya ruled Russia in the eighteenth century. [WRONG: named entity — English uses 'Catherine the Great' as the established anglicised name; 'Yekaterina Velikaya' is the untranslated Russian form not used in English historical writing]

chosen: The Olympic Games were held in Sochi.
rejected: The Olympic Games were held in Sochi city on Black Sea. [WRONG: addition — the translator added 'city on Black Sea' which is not present in the source sentence; translation must not add geographic descriptions absent from the original]

prompt: Антон Чехов написал пьесу Три сестры.
a_side: Антон Чехов написал пьесу Три сестры.
chosen: Anton Chekhov wrote the play Three Sisters.
rejected: Anton Chekhov wrote the play Tri Sestry. [WRONG: named entity — the title 'Три сестры' should be given as its established English translation 'Three Sisters'; keeping the Russian title 'Tri Sestry' is incorrect for a canonical work with an established English name]

chosen: Nicolaus Copernicus developed the heliocentric system.
rejected: Nikolai Kopernik discovered heliocentric system. [WRONG: named entity — the historical figure's name is 'Nicolaus Copernicus' in English; 'Nikolai Kopernik' is the Russian form; also 'the heliocentric system' requires the definite article]

prompt: Он катится как сыр в масле.
a_side: Он катится как сыр в масле.
chosen: He is living the life of Riley.
rejected: He rolls like a cheese in butter. [WRONG: literal calque — 'кататься как сыр в масле' is a Russian idiom meaning to live in comfort and luxury; its English equivalent is 'living the life of Riley' or 'living in clover'; the rejected side translates the image literally]

chosen: He promised the moon.
rejected: He promised three boxes full of goods. [WRONG: literal calque — 'обещать с три короба' is an idiom meaning to make excessive or unrealistic promises; its English equivalent is 'promised the moon' or 'promised everything under the sun'; the rejected side translates the archaic measurement literally]

prompt: У него семь пятниц на неделе.
a_side: У него семь пятниц на неделе.
chosen: He keeps changing his mind.
rejected: He has seven Fridays in one week. [WRONG: literal calque — 'семь пятниц на неделе' is a Russian idiom describing someone who constantly changes decisions; its English equivalent is 'keeps changing his mind'; the rejected side renders the days of the week literally]

chosen: He made a mountain out of a molehill.
rejected: He made an elephant out of a fly. [WRONG: literal calque — 'сделать из мухи слона' is a Russian idiom equivalent to the English 'make a mountain out of a molehill'; the rejected side translates the Russian image (fly → elephant) literally instead of finding the English equivalent]

prompt: Волков бояться — в лес не ходить.
a_side: Волков бояться — в лес не ходить.
chosen: Nothing ventured, nothing gained.
rejected: If you fear wolves you should not enter the forest. [WRONG: literal calque — this Russian proverb about risk and reward has the English equivalent 'nothing ventured, nothing gained'; the rejected side explains the proverb's scenario literally rather than using the established English equivalent]

prompt: Слово не воробей, вылетит — не поймаешь.
a_side: Слово не воробей, вылетит — не поймаешь.
chosen: A word once spoken cannot be taken back.
rejected: A word is not a sparrow, once it flies out you cannot catch it. [WRONG: literal calque — this Russian proverb about the permanence of spoken words has the English equivalent 'a word once spoken cannot be taken back'; the rejected side translates the sparrow metaphor literally rather than conveying the meaning]

prompt: Он говорит одно, а делает другое.
a_side: Он говорит одно, а делает другое.
chosen: He says one thing and does another.
rejected: He speaks one and makes other. [WRONG: literal calque — 'делает другое' is 'does another thing'; 'говорит одно' is 'says one thing'; 'makes other' is an incomplete and ungrammatical rendering]

prompt: Она сдала все экзамены на отлично.
a_side: Она сдала все экзамены на отлично.
chosen: She passed all her exams with top marks.
rejected: She gave all the exams excellently. [WRONG: mistranslation — 'сдать экзамен' means 'to pass an exam'; 'give an exam' means to administer it; also 'на отлично' means 'with top marks', not just 'excellently']

prompt: Он перешёл дорогу на красный свет.
a_side: Он перешёл дорогу на красный свет.
chosen: He crossed the road on a red light.
rejected: He crossed road on red. [WRONG: literal calque — 'дорогу' requires 'the road'; 'на красный свет' is 'on a red light'; dropping these words produces an incomplete and ungrammatical sentence]

chosen: The results were published in the newspaper.
rejected: Results was published in newspaper. [WRONG: morphological — plural subject 'results' requires the plural auxiliary 'were', not 'was'; also articles 'the' are required for specific known referents]

prompt: Она сделала вид, что не заметила его.
a_side: Она сделала вид, что не заметила его.
chosen: She pretended not to notice him.
rejected: She made appearance that she did not notice him. [WRONG: literal calque — 'сделать вид' is an idiom meaning 'to pretend'; 'made appearance' is a literal rendering of the Russian words that does not produce a natural English phrase]
